newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot natgas prices rise on storage refills.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas prices rise on storage refills.

text.p: Canadian natural gas prices were mostly firmer Tuesday as the need to refill storage counteracted the drop in heating demand, market sources said.

At the AECO storage hub, prices for Wednesday delivery climbed seven cents to C$1.76-1.77 per gigajoule (GJ) despite Tuesday's forecasts in Calgary calling for temperature highs of 14 degrees Celsius.
"NOVA drafted a lot last night," one Calgary-based source said, noting the approximate 300 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) taken off the system tightened the market and thereby propped up prices.
About 600 mmcfd of gas was injected into Alberta storage on Monday, he said, adding that he expected storage refills to taper off in the near-term.
May AECO was quoted at C$1.72-1.73 per GJ.
Storage buying also influenced prices at Sumas, Wash., where deals were reported done at $1.37-1.41 per million British thermal units (mmBtu), up three cents from Monday.
In the East, where storage levels hovered above a year ago, gas prices at Niagara in southern Ontario eased by about one cent to $2.25-2.28 per mmBtu.
